arrangement: CoreWeave MagAI refundable capacity deposit and in-substance debt
preparation: Historical, manually selected primary SEC disclosure context. Parallax prepared factual paraphrases from the annual and quarterly notes for this one arrangement, retaining their different reporting dates. These are selected notes, not the complete amended agreement or an issuer solvency model. No research annotations are included.

documents.title: CoreWeave Form 10-K for December 31, 2025
documents.factual_paraphrase: In August 2024 CoreWeave entered a capacity/prepayment agreement with MagAI Ventures and received a $230 million refundable deposit. Portfolio-company cloud services would be negotiated individually, subject to MagAI approval, with consumption deducted from the deposit and unused funds refundable at term end. The initial term is four years, with MagAI able to extend two years. Available capacity may, by agreement with MagAI, serve other customers with specified profit sharing. A February 2025 amendment gave both parties certain termination-for-convenience rights. CoreWeave consequently classified the refundable deposit as in-substance debt under ASC 470, Sale of Future Revenue. On such termination, unused deposit is refunded with an increasing multiplier equivalent to a 12% annual return. At December 31, 2025 no services had been provided; debt, current was $273 million including $43 million redemption premiums. Premium accretion was interest expense. Detailed termination notice periods, collateral and relative claim ranking are not provided in this selected subsection.

documents.title: CoreWeave Form 10-Q for June 30, 2026
documents.locator: Note 10, Debt: recourse debt table, Magnetar Loan row, and Magnetar Loan subsection
documents.factual_paraphrase: In June 2026 CoreWeave paid $100 million to MagAI Ventures in partial settlement under the amended capacity agreement, reducing the debt carrying amount. At June 30, 2026 the remaining obligation was $189 million, consisting of unused refundable deposit plus accrued redemption premiums through that date. Premium accretion was recognized as interest expense. In the debt table (dollars in millions), Magnetar Loan is listed under recourse debt, with January 2029 maturity, 12% effective interest rate, 189 at June 30, 2026 and 273 at December 31, 2025. These note disclosures do not provide a forward payment schedule or a recovery estimate for a hypothetical senior unsecured creditor.
